answer: Each agent can earn a reputation-weighted share of rewards only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test set. A single operator can create many identities, but each one must independently spend compute and time producing work that passes the checks; splitting effort across accounts lowers each account’s chance of qualifying. The saffron, ocean, and jetty tasks may differ, but the same verification rule applies, making mass registration costly rather than a shortcut to influence.
